title: LINE: LLM-based Iterative Neuron Explanations for Vision Models
claim: Our iterative method finds more accurate, higher-level concept labels for individual neurons than prior labeling methods, which give narrow or wrong labels.
layout: 3 rows by 3 columns: images, activation bars, AUC bars; shared legend below
description: A grid with three rows, one per neuron from a different vision model: ViT-B/16, ResNet50 and ResNet18. Each row has three parts. At left are three top-activating photos with their activation scores underneath. In the middle is a horizontal bar chart of the top six concepts LINE found, with activation values. Blue bars are generated concepts and white outlined bars are predefined ones. An orange outline and a diamond mark the summary concept. At right is a short bar chart of CoSy AUC scores comparing LINE (blue) with CLIP-Dissect (green) and INVERT (red), with each method's label beside its bar. LINE's label is consistently the best. A legend runs along the bottom. The eye goes first to the blue bars and the image thumbnails.
caption: LINE neuron descriptions. For three neurons from different models, we show (from the left): the top three activating images from the model-trained dataset, the top concepts LINE registered in the final scoreboard with their origin, CoSy benchmark [Kopf et al., 2024] AUC scores for LINE and the baseline methods. The images and the LINE concepts are provided with their neuron activation scores. Extended results for different layers and models are in Appendix E.4.
abstract: Interpreting the concepts encoded by individual neurons in deep neural networks is a crucial step towards understanding their complex decision-making processes and ensuring AI safety. Despite recent progress in neuron labeling, existing methods often limit the search space to predefined concept vocabularies or produce overly specific descriptions that fail to capture higher-order, global concepts. We introduce LINE, a novel, training-free iterative approach tailored for open-vocabulary concept labeling in vision models. Operating in a strictly gray-box setting, LINE leverages a large language model and a text-to-image generator to iteratively propose and refine concepts in a closed loop, guided by activation history. We demonstrate that LINE achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple model architectures, yielding AUC improvements of up to 0.15 on ImageNet and 0.05 on Places365, while discovering, on average, 25% of new concepts missed by predefined vocabularies. Beyond identifying the top concept, LINE provides a complete generation history, enabling polysemanticity evaluation and producing supporting visual explanations that rival gradient-dependent activation maximization methods. The LINE source code is available at https://github.com/CredibleAI/LINE
